title: Varden claims portal build kickoff
contextText: Build phase kickoff after discovery. Rosa back from leave.

segments.text: Welcome back, Rosa, and welcome to the build kickoff.
Thanks. I'm back, but on mornings only for now while I recover from the surgery. Ben stays my backup in the afternoons.
Glad you're back. Let's make the mornings count.
Mateo, there's one thing from the spike we need to discuss first.
Yes. In June we decided to rebuild the portal on top of the existing policy API. The spike showed the claims endpoints in that API can't support real-time status.
They batch overnight. There's no way to get a claim's status during the day.
Which is the whole point of the project. Status is thirty percent of our calls.
So my recommendation is to replace the policy API's claims endpoints with a new claims service, and keep the rest of the API.
That reverses what we decided in June.
It does, but for a reason we didn't know then.
Then we reverse it. We replace the claims endpoints with a new claims service.
I can live with that. The rest of the policy API stays.
Decided. Mateo, what do you need to write it up?
I'll write the architecture decision record by next Tuesday.
I want two claims handlers involved from the start as product champions.
Who picks them?
I'll nominate two claims handlers as product champions by August 14.
On budget, the build phase is approved at 1.4 million, with a ten percent contingency.
Good. My team will need a staging environment.
I'll include staging in the ADR.
Great. So: new claims service, ADR by next Tuesday, champions by August 14.

note.body:
# Varden claims portal build kickoff

**Date:** August 6
**Attendees:** Alex Rivera (Larkspur Labs), Hana Sato (Larkspur Labs), Mateo Rossi (Larkspur Labs), Rosa Delgado (Varden Insurance), Ben Adeyemi (Varden Insurance)

## Summary

Kickoff of the build phase for the Varden Insurance claims portal rebuild. Rosa is back from leave, working mornings only for now; Ben covers afternoons.

## Spike finding

- In June the team decided to rebuild the portal on top of the existing policy API.
- The integration spike showed the API's claims endpoints only batch overnight and cannot support real-time claim status during the day.
- Real-time status is the heart of the project: status checks are thirty percent of claims calls.

## Decisions

- **Reverse the June decision: replace the policy API's claims endpoints with a new claims service**, keeping the rest of the policy API. The reversal is based on the spike, which was not available in June.
- Two claims handlers will be involved from the start as product champions.

## Budget

The build phase is approved at 1.4 million with a ten percent contingency.

## Action items

- **Mateo Rossi** — write the architecture decision record by next Tuesday, including a staging environment for Ben's team.
- **Rosa Delgado** — nominate two claims handlers as product champions by August 14.

## Notes

- Rosa is on mornings only for now; schedule key decisions before noon.
